prerequisites: FONDAMENTI DI ANALISI DEI SEGNALI E TRASMISSIONE

learning_outcomes.text: Basic notions about the physical layer and digital modulations involved in point-to-point communications.
Planning and simulating a simple digital transmission system in view of bandwidth and power requirements.
Basic notions about wireless communications and about link budget.

Planning a point-to-point system made of multiple paths, by selecting the appropriate transmission technologies, and by conveniently dimensioning the system in terms of link budget and allocation of analog and/or digital repeaters.
Basic notions about cellular networks and about multiple access techniques in telecommunication networks.
Dimensioning a simple cellular system in view of capacity constraints.
Selecting appropriate access techniques in view of system requirements.
Basic notions about telecommunication network architectures. New-generation networks. MIMO systems
Planning simple solutions for access network management in 5G networks.
Planning simple solutions for core network management in 5G networks.
Planning simple new-generation telecommunication network architectures by selecting appropriate enabling technologies in view of the system requirements (i.e., bandwidth, power, and latency).
Basic notions about architectures and transmission technologies over communication networks: satellite communications, cellular networks, optical fibers, wireless technologies.
New generation networks. Main attributes of 5G networks.
Designing and simulating new-generation network architectures.
Selecting the enabling technologies more suited to a specific setting, optimizing the network configuration and resource allocation in view of bandwidth, power, and latency requirements.

syllabus_topics: Basic architecture of systems and telecommunication networks. Point-to-point communication model. Physical layer.
Transmission technologies. Optical fibers. Satellite communications. Wireless communications. Cellular networks.
Standard modulations: PSK and QAM. Geometric representation and performance evaluation. Bandwidth and power requirements.
Orthogonal modulations. Geometric representation and performance evaluation. Bandwidth and power requirements.
Exercises on digital modulations.
Computer-aided simulations on digital modulations.
Multipath and Doppler effects in wireless channels. Fading in mobile radiocommunications. Rayleigh model.
Evaluation of performance degradation in digital systems caused by fading. Countermeasures: Diversity techniques.
Analog and digital repeaters. The link budget problem.
Exercises on fading.
Exercises on link budget planning with analog repeaters.
Computer-aided simulations on digital systems affected by fading, with or without diversity techniques.
The “cellular” concept. Cell partitioning. Frequency reuse.
Cell allocation problems, dimensioning, and coverage. Near-far effect. Handover strategies.
Access techniques. Orthogonal techniques. TDMA. FDMA. Non-orthogonal access techniques.
Spread-spectrum techniques. CDMA. OFDM.
Dimensioning of a cellular system.
Computer-aided simulations on multiple access techniques.
Overview on different generation networks.
LTE networks and advanced LTE (LTE-A). Voice over LTE.
5G networks. Critical aspects of 5G networks and comparison with previous generations.
Access network. Radio aspects. Software Defined Radio.
Beamforming.
Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) systems.
Massive MIMO in 5G.
Computer-aided simulations of a simple MIMO system
5G Core Network.
Network softwarization. Software Defined Networks, Network Function Virtualization. Network Slicing in 5G.
The Edge concept. Wireless Edge. Edge Computing and advantages in terms of resources, latency, QoS.
Security issues in 5G.
Delay problems. Latency requirements. Low-latency in 5G.
Delay models
Planning and simulating an application covering aspects pertaining to access and/or core and/or edge network, Part 1.
Planning and simulating an application covering aspects pertaining to access and/or core and/or edge network, Part 2.
Planning and simulating an application covering aspects pertaining to access and/or core and/or edge network, Part 3.
Planning and simulating an application covering aspects pertaining to access and/or core and/or edge network, Part 4.
teaching_methods: Computer laboratory experiences focused on the simulation of communication systems

assessment_methods.method: Implementation of a simple simulator to solve a problem of design and allocation in a communication system

assessment_rules: The successful achievement of the learning outcomes will be assessed through a written examination consisting of exercises pertaining to the topics illustrated during the course, and the implementation of a simple simulator to solve a problem of design and allocation in a communication system. The final grade is a combined written and oral exam.
